title: 15 Years, 15 Stories: Netflix Celebrates Its Anniversary in Mexico With New Mexican Productions
summary: 15 new titles are coming to Netflix in the coming months, including series, films, documentaries, and reality shows.
body_markdown:
-


15 new titles are coming to Netflix in the coming months, including series, films, documentaries, and reality shows.


-


Netflix has produced and co-produced more than 200 titles in Mexico between 2016 and 2025, filming in more than 100 cities and generating an economic impact of more than 50 billion Mexican pesos in the country.


Download images


[HERE](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1coB2N9jDlnvbEzE_zLZdQZgWHyCE9PXu?usp=sharing) .


*Download-only links; please do not include them in your coverage.


Mexico City, September 10, 2026.-


Do you remember when you depended on the TV programming guide to decide what was on? In Mexico, that changed exactly 15 years ago. With the arrival of Netflix, the way people experienced television also changed: what to watch, when to watch it, and how to watch it. Binge-watching became a phenomenon, seasons could be finished in a single weekend, and new ways emerged to discover and enjoy stories from around the world.


And when it comes to milestones, 11 years ago, in 2015, Netflix premiered its first original production outside the United States:


Club de Cuervos


. It was a defining moment that marked the beginning of a new chapter for Mexican stories and opened the door to a decade of unforgettable characters, genres, and voices created in Mexico.


To celebrate its 15th anniversary in Mexico, Netflix is announcing


a new slate of 15 Mexican productions coming soon


: comedy, drama, and action series and films; documentaries exploring topics such as memory, identity, family, and everyday life; and unscripted formats that will put physical endurance, strategy, and the ability to deceive and betray to the test.


> “Celebrating 15 years in Mexico fills us with pride, but above all, with infinite gratitude to the creative community and to the millions of Mexicans who enjoy our content every day,”
>
>
> said
>
>
> Carolina Leconte, VP of Content for Mexico and Licensing for Latin America at Netflix
>
>
> . “
>
>
> The 15 productions we are announcing today celebrate our history in the country, but they are also an invitation to keep exploring: new genres, new voices, and new ways of telling the stories of who we are. What excites us most about Mexico is that there is still so much left to discover.”


## Talent and Industry: Growing with Mexico


Behind every “Are you still watching?”, there is a vibrant creative ecosystem and a story of collaboration that has been growing alongside Mexico for more than a decade. These figures reflect the impact of the creative partnership between Netflix and the country from 2016 to 2025:


-


More than 50 billion Mexican pesos


(equivalent to more than $2.7 billion) have been contributed to Mexico’s GDP as a result of Netflix’s investments and productions in the country.


-


More than 200 titles have been produced or co-produced in the country


, in collaboration with more than 50 Mexican production companies.


-


More than 15,000 cast and crew members


have participated in these productions, in addition to more than 20,000 extras and other daily hires.


-


More than 100 cities and towns across Mexico


have served as filming locations for these productions.


-


Approximately 50% of filming locations have been outside Mexico City


, bringing stories and audiovisual production to places such as Guadalajara, Puerto Escondido, San Miguel de Allende, Boca del Río, Hermosillo, and Tijuana.


Meet the 15 upcoming productions and


[here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1CY7HKin9dbXL3WtU9_xFirs2y3V47nJD/view?usp=drive_link) are the technical details for the titles:


Surviving Hurricane Otis


(film):


In the middle of the ocean, two brothers fight to survive Hurricane Otis off the coast of Acapulco. A story of brotherhood, inequality, and extreme courage, in which their love for each other becomes their only hope.


Director:


Jorge Michel Grau


Cast:


Benny Emmanuel, Kristyan Ferrer, Mónica del Carmen, Mónica Jiménez, Gonzalo Vega, and Andrew Leland.


---


Counterattack


(film):


A new installment that expands the universe of


Contraataque


, the action film released on February 28, 2025, which became one of Netflix’s most-watched Mexican productions.


Director:


Chava Cartas


---


El enemigo del pueblo


(film):


In Mexico in 1993, Pedro Azcona, a high school student at a school run by the Legionaries of Christ, embarks on an anarchist dream and joins the Zapatista revolution. Years later, he looks back on his adolescence from a place of success and privilege — the very things he fought against as a teenager.


Director:


Luis Estrada


Cast:


Emiliano Lach, Alfonso Herrera, Cassandra Ciangherotti, José Ramón Soroiz, Rafaella López, Tessa Ía, Naian González Norvind, and Mauricio Isaac.


---


35 días


(film):


Julián is a loving and remarkable father. His drinking has gradually taken up more and more space in his life, until it brings him to rock bottom. During 35 days in rehabilitation, Julián begins the journey back to himself and to his family. A story about love, second chances, and the possibility of being present again for the people we love most.


Director:


Kyzza Terrazas


Production Company:


Woo Films


Cast:


Mauricio Ochmann, Zuria Vega, Diana Bovio, Eme MalaFe, Daniel Tovar, Rafaella López, Fernando Cattori, José Carlos Rodríguez, and Anabel Ferreira.


---


Ashes


(film):


In search of a better life, Lucila travels with her brother Diego from Mexico to reunite with their mother in Madrid, where she has spent the past eight years working illegally to support them. When they arrive, the life awaiting them proves harder than they imagined.


Director:


Diego Luna


Cast:


Luisa Huertas, Guillermo Rios, Sergio Bautista, Benny Emmanuel, Teresa Lozano, and Adriana Jacomé.


---


Dogman


(series):


Eric is a young man trapped in a job he does not like and a family that depends on him. When he accidentally ends up in a wrestling ring, Dogman is born: a symbol of the frustration and rebellion of a generation without a future. He must find a balance between who he is and the person behind the mask before Dogman consumes him completely.


Director:


Sebastián Sariñana (showrunner), Cris Gris


Production Company:


La Granja


Cast:


Xiunel Castillo, Jorge Luis Alcantar (Santos Escobar), Roberto Aguilar, Andrea Chaparro, Lizeth Selene, Paola Fernández, Fermín Martínez, Nashla Aguilar, Juan Carlos Medellín, Alexis Valdés, Marco León, and Axel Arenas.


---


Un tipo de cuidado


(series):


Valentín Fernández is a Mexican film actor whose career is on the decline. After losing his apartment, he is forced to move in with the family of his only son, who died a year ago and with whom Valentín did not have a very good relationship. This family turns out to be what everyone needs.


Director:


Samuel Kishi Lopo


Production Company:


The Immigrant


Cast:


Damián Alcázar and Diana Bovio.


---


La madre perfecta


(series):


Catalina and Víctor San Miguel have the life they always dreamed of, until one day a body appears on the seabed. Catalina’s identity could be a lie, and uncovering the truth could cost her her life.


Directors:


Felipe Cano & José Ramón Chávez


Cast:


Camila Sodi, Osvaldo Benavides, Macarena García, Edu Maruri, Valentina Buzzurro, Luis de la Rosa, Naian González Norvid, Romina Poza, María Uriarte, Carlo Basabe, Sofía Espinosa, Mariano Palacios, Daniella Reyes, and Michael Ronda.


---


Rosario Tijeras. Season 6


(series):


Rosario must leave everything she knows behind to infiltrate one of the most powerful criminal organizations in the country. On this mission, she discovers that surviving means facing an enemy as intelligent as they are unpredictable — one capable of testing her convictions, her strength, and even her heart.


Directors:


Danny Gavidia, David Romay, and Sergio Siruela


Cast:


Bárbara de Regil.


---


Canelo Álvarez


(documentary):


Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez enters the fight that will define his legacy: the epic trilogy against Gennady “GGG” Golovkin. Along the way, Canelo proudly and honorably shares the values that define him.


Director:


Juan Camilo Cruz


Production:


Unanimous Media


Cast:


Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez.


---


Liliana’s Invincible Summer


(documentary)


:


Based on the book of the same name, the documentary weaves together memory and an investigation into the murder of Liliana Rivera Garza, while revealing how the absence of the term femicide at the time contributed to decades of impunity and silence.


Directors:


Inna Payán and Samuel Kishi.


---


Marcos. Another World Is Possible


(documentary):


Through the figure of Subcomandante Marcos, this documentary delves into the struggle of the Zapatista communities that, more than 30 years later, continue building their own way of resisting and living in the mountains of Chiapas.


Director:


Diego Enrique Osorno


Production Company:


Detective.


---


Keiko


(documentary):


Keiko was the beloved mascot of an entire generation and spent years living in a world designed by humans. What began as the dream of thousands of children to see her return to the ocean became one of the most ambitious and controversial animal-release experiments in history.


Director:


Santiago Fábregas


Production Companies:


Mezcla and The Lift Films.


---


Physical 100: Mexico


(reality):


In a pre-Hispanic arena, 100 participants will compete to discover who possesses the best physical abilities. All participants will compete under the same conditions and with the same goal: to defeat the other 99.


Production:


EndemolShine Boomdog.


---


Million Dollar Secret


(unscripted):


The “Dos caras” estate is a place where lying, betraying, and conspiring are not only allowed — they are the only way to win a million-dollar prize. Adela Micha is ready to welcome 12 celebrities who are willing to do whatever it takes to succeed.


Production:


EndemolShine Boomdog.
